Shopify Storefront Proposal

Jr. RangerLand — Shopify Storefront Proposal

Client: Jr. RangerLand — educational books, games, puzzles & outdoor gear for kids
Prepared by: LitOS/LitGroup
Date: August 13, 2026
1

Proposed scope

1.1 Platform

Move the storefront to Shopify.

This proposal covers Shopify design & development only. Backend data migration (products, orders, customers) is not included — that's handled by a separate team, LitExtension (a sister brand), who provide their own estimate and quote once the volume to migrate is known.

SEO / onsite optimization — keeping existing rankings and product discoverability on the new store — sits with that same team, since it's driven by URL redirect mapping (old URLs → new Shopify URLs) as part of the data migration.

1.2 Theme

Foundation theme: Ella — free through the Litos/HaloThemes partnership.

Ella ships with a built-in wishlist and a wide range of header, collection and product-page layouts, which covers several items below without custom development. Both options are built by customizing Ella — not a rebuild from scratch — keeping the current color palette and overall look and feel of the store.

1.3 Core build

Included in both options:

  • Theme selection & customization — Ella configured to carry over the existing brand palette and overall look/feel.
  • Page templates & layout build — homepage, About Us page, and a product page template applied across all 117 product pages.
  • Responsive storefront — verified on desktop, tablet and mobile.
  • Full storefront review & testing before launch, so everything is verified working before the store goes live.

1.4 Front-end improvements

Included in both options.

Header & navigation

  • Login and cart moved to a single right-hand cluster, search field narrowed, and the main menu consolidated onto one row.
  • Menu items grouped into shorter parent categories rather than listed flat — e.g. Games & Fun containing Board Games, Card Games, Puzzles.
  • Top announcement bar reduced in height, with more visual weight given to the menu.

Homepage

  • Simplified layout — fewer sections and elements, with a clearer path through the page. This is a priority for the store.
  • The homepage leads with the main collections rather than individual products, so a category like hats opens into its full range instead of showing one item.
  • Hero redesigned — typography aligned with the rest of the site, and lifestyle photography showing the products in use (kids wearing the hats, carrying the bags), which reads more clearly than product-only imagery.
  • Narrow single-purpose sections consolidated into collection sections, so each block earns its space.
  • The Contact Us block removed from the homepage.
  • The three banner sections redesigned and recolored so the homepage reads as one consistent palette.

Color & visual style

  • Reduce the number of colors in use and shift toward a brighter, fresher palette. Young children respond more strongly to saturated color and high contrast than to muted tones, and a bright palette matches the playful, creative character of educational toys and children's books. It also keeps the page looking deliberate and easy for parents to scan, with action elements — add to cart, promotions — standing out more clearly.
  • Softer styling on card and content blocks — rounded corners, lighter shadows and more generous spacing, in place of the current hard-edged treatment.
  • Buttons restyled to a rounded, friendlier shape in keeping with a children's brand.

Product cards

  • Hover treatment replaced — the current effect crops the image corners. Instead, a border animation with the title sliding up from the bottom of the card, or a comparable effect.
  • Wishlist placed on the same row as Add to Cart, rather than on a separate line below it.

Collection pages

  • Price filter added alongside the existing filters.
  • Filters stick to the viewport on scroll, or a filter button appears on scroll, so products stay easy to narrow down further down a long collection.
  • On mobile, tapping Filter opens a popup rather than expanding inline and pushing the products down the page.

Product page

  • Product video enlarged so it reads as part of the page rather than a thumbnail.
  • Frequently Bought Together — related products suggested on the product page.
  • Bundle / Combo — multiple products offered together at a set price, to lift average order value.

Footer

Rebuilt with a clear column structure, brand styling and full navigation, in place of the current plain link grid.

Responsive fixes

Header, hero and collection sections currently render incorrectly on mobile. All three are rebuilt to display correctly across screen sizes.

1.5 Option 2 — full design pass

Option 2 adds a dedicated design phase ahead of the build. Three pages are designed as complete mockups — homepage, collection page and product page — covering full visual direction, typography, color system, section layouts and component styling, approved before any code is written. Remaining pages, including About Us, are built to that same design system without separate mockups.

Option 1 delivers the same scope, implemented directly on Ella's existing components and styling rather than from custom page designs.

1.6 Product listing layout

The current collection pages use a table-format listing where quantities for several products can be entered and added to the cart in one action:

  • https://rangerland.com/art-kits?mode=table
  • https://rangerland.com/art-kits?mode=table

The recommendation is to build on Ella's standard collection layout (reference) — it supports the same custom product text as the current listing, and saves both cost and time. The one difference: quantity is set for one product at a time, so adding a second product means moving to that product's card rather than filling in several quantities at once. In practice this has minimal impact on the shopping experience.

Reproducing the current table-format listing requires custom development: +10h, +$300, on top of either option.
